solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Highest price to pay when initially cut

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: initially points at the opening letter of each of the two words just before it

parts.note: first letter of pay
first letter of when
to hack is to cut roughly

explanation.surface: A shopper wonders what is the most they will have to pay once the price is first reduced.
explanation.walkthrough: TOP WHACK is British slang for the top rate or highest price.
explanation.definitionFit: In British slang a whack is a share or amount paid, so the top whack is the maximum charge.

clue.text: It's grabbed by ultra weird puppet?

indicators.note: grabbed by means held inside the other letters
weird means strange, so the letters are put in a strange order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone asks if a strange puppet is gripped by something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Puppet' is an adjective here, as in a puppet ruler.
explanation.definitionFit: A titular ruler holds the title only, with no real power, like a puppet government.

clue.text: Love the sound of noses

indicators.note: the sound of means we want a word that is spoken alike, not spelt alike

parts.note: noses as a verb, as in noses into others' business

explanation.surface: Someone adores the sound of noses, perhaps sniffing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Noses' looks like a noun, but it is the verb meaning snoops.
explanation.definitionFit: To prize something is to value it highly, to love it.

clue.text: It will blow up, presumably

parts.note: surface reading: an explosive that will detonate
setter's reading: something tall and explosive would naturally blow upwards, so the first word of the answer explains 'up'

explanation.walkthrough: The joke is that 'high' suggests upward, so an explosive that is high must blow up.
explanation.definitionFit: A high explosive is a powerful detonating material such as TNT.

clue.text: "Blue sky", said pirate

indicators.note: said means the quoted words are spoken, and the sound gives the answer

parts.note: blue means smutty or coarse, and the sky is the air

explanation.surface: A pirate remarks on the blue sky.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Blue' is not a colour here: a blue joke is a rude one.
explanation.definitionFit: A corsair was a pirate, especially of the Barbary coast.

clue.text: When talking, take off jumper

indicators.note: when talking means we judge the words by how they are spoken, not spelt

parts.note: to take off is to run away

explanation.surface: Instructions for removing a sweater while chatting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jumper' reads as a British sweater, which fits 'take off', but it is the insect that jumps.
explanation.definitionFit: The insect is famous for leaping huge distances relative to its size, so it is a jumper.

clue.text: Old comic sold as new comic

indicators.note: comic means funny or ridiculous, so the letters are made a mess of

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A stale comedian is passed off as a fresh one.
explanation.walkthrough: Les Dawson was a British comedian, famous for deadpan mother-in-law jokes, who died in 1993.
explanation.definitionFit: Les Dawson was a British comedian of a past era, so an old comic.

clue.text: A jar full of mostly mellow fruit

indicators.note: mostly means not all of the word, so its last letter is dropped

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: full of means the jar holds the next part inside it

parts.note: a pot is a jar
rich means mellow, as of a flavour, minus its last letter

explanation.surface: A jar of nearly ripe fruit.
explanation.definitionFit: An apricot is a soft orange stone fruit.

clue.text: Ringo Starr involved with breast feeding group

indicators.note: feeding means one part goes into the middle of the other, as food goes in
involved suggests something tangled up, so the former Beatle's name is jumbled

parts.note: the Beatles drummer's name, letter for letter
the breast is the chest

explanation.surface: The Beatles drummer gets mixed up with a breastfeeding support group.
explanation.definitionFit: A string orchestra is a group of musicians playing only bowed string instruments.

clue.text: I pick a horse up on country trip

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the words are read bottom to top

parts.note: taken as written
to cull is to pick out or select
taken as written
horse is slang for heroin, abbreviated H
a nation is a country

explanation.surface: A traveller chooses a horse for a trip across the country.
explanation.walkthrough: Only the first part is turned round; NATION follows as written.
explanation.definitionFit: A trip is a drug-induced experience full of things that are not really there.

clue.text: Garment to take to the cleaners

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a warm fleecy jacket
second meaning: to swindle someone out of money

explanation.surface: A piece of clothing needing to go to the dry cleaner.
explanation.walkthrough: The dry cleaner fits the garment, but 'take to the cleaners' is an idiom for robbing someone.
explanation.definitionFit: A fleece is a soft warm jacket, and to fleece someone is to cheat them of money.

clue.text: Bond completely frozen, and almost trapped

indicators.note: almost means the word falls one letter short, so its last letter goes

parts.note: all means completely, as in all alone

indicators.note: trapped means held inside another word

parts.note: frozen water is ice
and without its last letter

explanation.surface: A man named Bond is caught in the cold and held prisoner, like a spy in a thriller.
explanation.definitionFit: An alliance is a bond or union formed between parties.

clue.text: Lip balm's first applied to lip

indicators.note: first picks out only the opening letter of the word before it

parts.note: opening letter of balm
the lip of a cup is its rim

explanation.surface: Instructions for putting on lip balm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lip balm' reads as one cosmetic, but Lip is the definition and balm gives one letter.
explanation.definitionFit: The brim of a vessel or hat is its edge or lip.

clue.text: Pig runs away, seeing snake

indicators.note: runs away means the cricket abbreviation for runs leaves the word

parts.note: a boar is a pig
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: A pig flees in fright at the sight of a snake.
explanation.definitionFit: A boa is a large constricting snake.

clue.text: Partners cutting low quality feldspar

indicators.note: cutting means slicing into the middle of the other words

parts.note: a cow lows, i.e. moos
North and South are partners at bridge
tone is a quality, as of sound

explanation.surface: Business partners cut costs by selling poor-quality minerals.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Low' is the verb for a cow's call, not an adjective of 'quality'.
explanation.definitionFit: Moonstone is a pearly, translucent variety of feldspar used as a gem.

clue.text: A rather round one's a bonus

parts.note: per means a, as in five pounds a head

indicators.note: round means one word goes around the other, enclosing it

parts.note: quite means rather, as in quite good
one is I, and the 's adds S

explanation.surface: A plump person is said to be a real bonus.
explanation.definitionFit: A perquisite, or perk, is an extra benefit received on top of pay.

clue.text: The day before still hasn't finished

indicators.note: hasn't finished means the word stops before its last letter

parts.note: even as in even more: still

explanation.surface: Something begun the day before is still incomplete.
explanation.definitionFit: The eve of an event is the day or evening just before it, as in Christmas Eve.

clue.text: In one second, Italian lady reverses old age

indicators.note: reverses means the whole string built so far is read from the end

parts.note: taken as written
Roman numeral one
a mo is a moment, a second
donna is Italian for lady

explanation.surface: An Italian woman instantly turns back the clock on ageing.
explanation.walkthrough: Besides AD in dates, ANNO DOMINI is a jokey British phrase for advancing years.
explanation.definitionFit: Anno Domini is humorously used to mean the effects of advancing years, i.e. old age.

clue.text: One present is not two presents

parts.note: the first present: present in time, at this moment
the second present: present in place, at this spot

explanation.surface: A riddle about how one gift differs from two gifts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Presents' looks like gifts; the clue means being present, in time and in place.
explanation.definitionFit: Nowhere is the place where anyone present cannot be, since being present means being somewhere.

clue.text: Wilfred's house in one part of windmill

parts.note: Roman numeral one

indicators.note: in places one word inside the other

parts.note: the vanes are the sails of a windmill
HO is the abbreviation for house

explanation.surface: Someone named Wilfred lives in part of a windmill.
explanation.walkthrough: Wilfred of Ivanhoe is the hero of Walter Scott's novel, so his name defines the title.
explanation.definitionFit: Ivanhoe is the knight Wilfred of Ivanhoe, title character of Scott's historical novel.

clue.text: A, B, C, D, F or G

definitions.text: A, B, C, D, F or G

wordplay.words: A, B, C, D, F or G
wordplay.note: the letters from A to G with one gap

explanation.surface: A list of grades or letters from the start of the alphabet, with one oddly missing.
explanation.walkthrough: The list runs A to G but skips E, so it is 'not E'; and each letter in it names a musical note.
explanation.definitionFit: A to G are the letter names of the musical notes, so any one is a note.

clue.text: Add lightweight fences to scrap

indicators.note: fences means encloses, as a fence goes round a field

parts.note: thin means slight or lightweight
a scrap is a fight or row

explanation.surface: Lightweight fencing is added to the scrap heap.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Scrap' looks like waste metal; it is a quarrel.
explanation.definitionFit: To throw in is to add something extra, often free, as in a sale.

clue.text: A tackle cuts returned cross

indicators.note: returned means sent back, so the phrase is read in the opposite direction

parts.note: taken as written
tackle is gear or kit
saws as a verb means cuts

explanation.surface: A rough football challenge leaves cuts and an angry, returning player.
explanation.definitionFit: The swastika is a hooked cross, the Nazi emblem and an ancient symbol.

clue.text: Reject most of panel in Lincoln

indicators.note: most of means nearly all, so the last letter is left off
in places one word inside the other

parts.note: Abe is Abraham Lincoln's short name
a jury is a panel, minus its last letter

explanation.surface: Most of a jury in the city of Lincoln reject something.
explanation.definitionFit: To abjure is to renounce or reject solemnly.

clue.text: Traitor not quite right to frame lawyer

indicators.note: not quite means a little short, so the last letter is dropped
to frame means to go around, like a picture frame

parts.note: just means right or fair, minus its last letter
a DA is a district attorney, an American lawyer

explanation.surface: A traitor plots to frame a lawyer, which is not quite right.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Frame' looks like falsely accusing; it means surround.
explanation.definitionFit: Judas Iscariot betrayed Jesus, so his name is a byword for a traitor.

clue.text: Party — free do?

parts.note: surface reading: a party, and a free event to go to
setter's reading: as a verb, to party is to relax; and freeing a hairdo means untying it so it falls loose

explanation.walkthrough: 'Free do' looks like a party with no charge; read 'do' as a hairdo set free, which is what the idiom pictures.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to relax and enjoy yourself without inhibition, which is what partying is.

clue.text: Views of earth all right

parts.note: E is the abbreviation for earth
yes as agreement: all right

explanation.surface: Pictures of the planet are deemed acceptable.
explanation.definitionFit: Eyes means opinion, as in 'in the eyes of the law', the same sense as views.

clue.text: Poet X's name — curious, on reflection

parts.note: Roman numeral X is ten
N is the abbreviation for name

indicators.note: on reflection means seen as in a mirror, so the word is backwards

parts.note: nosy means inquisitive

explanation.surface: Someone thinks about the odd name of a poet known only as X.
explanation.definitionFit: Alfred, Lord Tennyson was the Victorian Poet Laureate.
